title: Add canonical lexicon enforcement linter
summary: Add deterministic lexicon enforcement so user-facing docs, command help, tool schemas, skills, and validation reports use active canonical vocabulary and reject unused terms except explicit compatibility aliases.

goal.outcome: The canonical pruned lexicon is enforceable and unused quality/surface terms cannot re-enter user docs or agent guidance without explicit compatibility metadata.
acceptance: A lexicon linter reads active canonical terms, legacy compatibility aliases, and banned/removed terms from `.codewiki/kb/lexicon.md` or source-owned config.
The linter flags user-facing docs, command help, tool labels/descriptions, skills, generated views, and validation reports that use removed terms such as audit/proof/checks as canonical vocabulary.
Compatibility contexts for legacy source fields, file paths, current command aliases, and migration docs are explicit and narrow.
Linter output uses gateway/gate/linter/test/validation/evidence terminology in new messages where feasible while preserving backward-compatible profile names if required by source.
Tests cover allowed compatibility usage, rejected user-facing usage, and lexicon drift caused by adding unused terms.
non_goals: Do not rename every legacy source file or JSON schema field in this task unless needed for linter enforcement.
Do not delete compatibility aliases before the six-tool and command migrations land.
Do not make lexicon enforcement rely on generated graph output only.
Do not block documentation that explicitly describes a migration alias with approved rationale.
verification: wiki_gate/task-close linters for source-contract, stale-reference, changed, and horizontal-alignment
